candidates.exact_span: Unless otherwise indicated in this permit, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or pollutant parameter is sufficiently sensitive (as defined above) and the analytical test result is less than the MQL, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the MQL is 'sufficiently sensitive' and whether sub-MQL results may be reported as zero on DMRs determines the numeric value used for limit comparison (A) and how sub-threshold analytical results are classified versus true zero or missing evidence (C). The 'unless otherwise indicated' qualifier also affects whether this rule applies to a given parameter.

candidates.exact_span: Furthermore, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or parameter is not sufficiently sensitive, but the analytical test result is less than the published ML from a sufficiently sensitive method, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This alternate zero-reporting pathway applies when the Region 6 MQL is not sufficiently sensitive but a result falls below the published ML of a sensitive method. Different interpretations of which method/ML governs change the reported DMR value used for compliance comparison (A) and whether a non-detect is treated as a reported zero versus an unresolved or special no-data state (C).

candidates.exact_span: B. 24-HOUR ORAL REPORTING: DAILY MAXIMUM LIMITATION VIOLATIONS
candidates.computation_change_reason: The 24-hour oral-reporting window defines a time-bound reporting obligation triggered by daily maximum limit violations; interpreting when the clock starts or what constitutes timely reporting changes whether the monitoring/reporting obligation for FY2025 is met, not required, or unresolved (B).

candidates.exact_span: Under the provisions of Part III.D.7.b.(3) of this permit, violations of daily maximum limitations for the following pollutants shall be reported orally to EPA Region 6, Compliance and Assurance Division, Water Enforcement Branch (6EN-W), Dallas, Texas, and concurrently to NMED
candidates.computation_change_reason: This clause ties oral reporting to violations of daily maximum limitations, confirming those limits are enforceable comparators (A) and imposing a conditional reporting requirement whose applicability depends on interpreting 'violations,' which pollutants are covered by 'the following pollutants,' and the cross-referenced Part III.D.7.b.(3) provisions (B).
